text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: Not reliably estimable from these facts

An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence of sex bias. Neither the successful candidate’s sex nor the brief announcement establishes that you were better qualified against the selection criteria. A numerical probability would be invented.

Follow up your request for written reasons. Ask for the selection criteria, their weighting, your assessment and how the appointment met those criteria. Check applicable response deadlines and complaint time limits; these depend on jurisdiction.

Raise sex discrimination if concrete evidence emerges—for example, sex-based remarks or inconsistent treatment linked to sex. For now, focus on the decision-making process, not the panel’s composition.
